proves: a border is the ring between the border box and the padding box, inside the box, with both rings rounded
cases: box 1: uniform 4px border, 12px radius - one ring fill, no clip
box 2: widths top 2 right 8 bottom 5 left 0, radii tl 20 tr 0 br 10 bl 4, one edge taking border_color_all
box 3: 24px radius against widths differing five to one, so the arcs and the corner transitions are unmissable
checkable: the border is INSIDE the box. Box 1's 4px border spans x 8..127 of a box at 8..127; a stroke centred on the box edge would span 6..129 and hang half outside, which is what this pinned before.
also-checkable: box 2's red top edge starts at y=21 at its left end and y=20 at its right, following the 20px top-left arc. A border ignoring the radius is flat at one y across the whole width.
specification: CSS Backgrounds 3 5.2 for the inner radii (each axis reduced by that side's width, floored at zero) and 4.4 for the corner transition (a straight line from the outer corner point to the inner corner point, so unequal widths move the join without it being computed)
status: target, not a limitation. This image was previously accepted showing square border corners around a rounded fill and a stroke hanging outside the box; both were wrong and both are fixed.
